column4: Same extreme close-up composition and framing as the first reference: a porcelain doll's open eye, orange hair across the forehead, flower ornament at the corner, eyelashes drawn as ink lines, but in the iris the reflection is now the dawn sky from the third reference: inside the pupil-sized circle, flat dusty blue sky with a few sheep-shaped peach clouds and a hint of a rising sun, hard flat edges. The eye is wide open with a calm, hopeful look. No stained glass window, no figure, no strings in the reflection. The dusty blue and peach exist ONLY inside that reflection circle, everything else stays orange, ivory and coal. No text.

Wide view from the cathedral doorway down the nave toward the stage, camera locked, same nave and pews as the first reference. The hooded congregation kneels in the pews with bowed heads, seen from behind, as in the first reference. The nave floor in the foreground is strewn with fragments of broken stained glass and a pile of discarded porcelain doll heads with orange hair (second and third references), beside an empty hollow porcelain doll shell lying on its side. At the top right of the frame a large bare ball-jointed porcelain hand (fourth reference) hangs down from above, fingers slack and open. No threads, no text.
